specialists.label: React and frontend systems
specialists.summary: Apply the existing workflow to React interfaces, reusable components, responsive behaviour and frontend performance.
useWhen: React or Next.js components, application routes, state-driven UI or frontend regressions are in scope.
Shared design tokens, component APIs or rendering performance affect the requested change.
avoidWhen: The task is only static content conversion with no React runtime.
acceptance: Affected user journeys work at the required viewport and theme states.
State and component ownership match the existing architecture.
Relevant build, type and interaction evidence is recorded; visual review is separate.

specialists.label: Editors, registries and persistent schemas
specialists.summary: Preserve native widget models, nested editability, preset inheritance and persistent tree/configuration semantics across every editor surface.
useWhen: A visual editor, page builder, structured tree, widget registry or saved workspace is changing.
Document schemas, settings persistence, selection, undo/redo or import/export contracts are involved.
avoidWhen: The page is a static presentation with no editable document model.
acceptance: Registry, inspector, renderer and export agree on each supported field and default.
Edit-save-reload-export-import preserves nested relationships, stable identity and intended preset overrides.
Existing documents survive migration; unsupported fields and malformed input remain visible in diagnostics.

specialists.label: WordPress and WooCommerce
specialists.summary: Use WordPress and commerce-specific lifecycle, data, permissions and compatibility checks.
useWhen: A WordPress theme, plugin, block, REST integration or WooCommerce extension is in scope.
Content storage, custom checkout/order behaviour or PHP/JavaScript integration depends on WordPress.
avoidWhen: Only WHMCS is affected; there is no WordPress/WooCommerce component or integration.
The project has no WordPress runtime or compatibility requirement.
acceptance: The changed extension loads and behaves on the declared WordPress/PHP/WooCommerce versions.
Relevant authorised and unauthorised requests behave correctly.
Lifecycle and data changes preserve existing site/store behaviour and intended data.

specialists.label: WHMCS modules and client-area systems
specialists.summary: Assess and implement WHMCS extensions with verified hook contracts, lifecycle and account boundaries.
useWhen: The task changes a WHMCS addon, hook, client-area template, API integration or account workflow.
Rate limits, billing/account behaviour or module lifecycle depends on WHMCS.
avoidWhen: The task affects only WordPress/WooCommerce or generic PHP, with no WHMCS integration.
Only marketing-page copy changes and no WHMCS integration is affected.
acceptance: The relevant hook/module executes on the declared host version.
Account and admin boundaries are exercised with permitted and denied cases.
Repeat requests, concurrency and upgrade behaviour match the requested policy.

specialists.label: Plugins, skills and MCP applications
specialists.summary: Evolve plugin instructions, routers and tool/host contracts from evidence while preserving identity, explicit scope, compatibility and release provenance.
useWhen: A plugin, skill catalogue, command router, MCP server or ChatGPT app is being built or changed.
Tool descriptors, manifests, widget bridges or native-host contracts affect the requested behaviour.
avoidWhen: The task only invokes an existing plugin to perform unrelated application work.
No plugin, tool or host integration is in the actual scope.
acceptance: Catalogue entries, handler paths and portable/native route semantics resolve consistently, including preserved explicit invocations.
Changes retain identity, scope, prompts, configurations and assets outside the authorized delta; private usage history is excluded.
Realistic behavior and clean-package checks are recorded separately from guarded release/read-back and untested host activation.

specialists.label: Browser evidence and website extraction
specialists.summary: Ground reconstruction and UI repair in identified source versions, asset dependencies and comparable rendered/interactive states.
useWhen: The task extracts, rebuilds or diagnoses an existing website or browser interface.
Saved HTML/assets, screenshots, live page behaviour or browser-only failures are evidence.
avoidWhen: The task is a public factual lookup with no need to interact with a page.
A native application is the target and the available browser cannot observe it.
acceptance: Page/state/asset inventory identifies exact sources, output revisions and inaccessible targets.
Source and output are compared under recorded viewport/theme/font/control conditions.
Affected interactions and standalone exports are exercised; still screenshots do not stand in for motion or native-editor evidence.

specialists.label: Native YAML and archive conversion
specialists.summary: Map supplied HTML and the current kit to genuinely editable native widgets, presets and complete import packages with explicit custom-code exceptions.
useWhen: A supplied native YAML kit or receiving editor contract governs conversion of HTML, design-system sections or structured bundles.
Editable cards/products/tabs, preset variables, custom-code restrictions or archive/import compatibility are acceptance requirements.
avoidWhen: Only a static screenshot or prose explanation is needed.
No receiving schema/import contract can be obtained; report the gap before claiming compatible native output.
acceptance: The current kit and every requested section reconcile with a supported widget/field/capability mapping.
Custom HTML stays inside the explicit exception allowlist; presets, assets and nested editability are preserved.
Parsing, schema checks, actual editor import and rendered parity are reported as separate evidence levels.

specialists.label: Structured content and technical SEO
specialists.summary: Build and migrate source-grounded content collections with real destinations, preserved approved copy, coherent presentation and validated metadata/schema.
useWhen: Markdown/MDX content, seo.yaml/schema.yaml, article migrations or generated service pages are in scope.
Canonical URLs, sitemaps, redirects, internal links or structured-data output are affected.
avoidWhen: The task requests only general marketing strategy with no implementation or content artefact.
acceptance: Every requested content item maps to a produced destination or explicit exception; absent content is not invented to fill navigation.
Approved headings, code, assets and required content variants survive conversion and agree with visible output.
Metadata/schema/internal links validate against current content and canonical routes without unsupported product or ranking claims.

specialists.label: Python automation and data pipelines
specialists.summary: Build resumable data processing with validated inputs, explicit failures and reconciled outputs.
useWhen: Python scripts, API ingestion, scraping outputs, transformations or automation pipelines are changing.
Pagination, retries, checkpoints, data contracts or partial failure affect correctness.
avoidWhen: The project has no Python/data-processing component.
acceptance: Representative real input produces schema-valid, reconciled output.
Reruns, partial failures and pagination do not silently lose or duplicate data.
Existing runtime/tooling and externally visible data contracts remain compatible.

specialists.label: Database schemas and data integrity
specialists.summary: Apply engine-specific checks to migrations, queries, tenant access, locks and data compatibility.
useWhen: SQL/schema changes, query behaviour, data access rules or database performance are in scope.
A migration, import, restore or concurrency issue can affect persisted data.
avoidWhen: The change is purely presentational and does not alter data access.
acceptance: Schema/query changes match the detected engine and migration tooling.
Data invariants, access boundaries and relevant concurrency behaviour hold.
Migration and rollback/recovery evidence is appropriate to the authorised environment.

specialists.label: Infrastructure and deployment configuration
specialists.summary: Ground infrastructure changes in provider versions, actual state, execution mode and recovery evidence.
useWhen: Server/container configuration, infrastructure as code, CI deployment or runtime operations are changing.
Networking, secrets, storage, provisioning or service health affect the requested result.
avoidWhen: The task is only application UI/content work with no infrastructure impact.
acceptance: Configuration validates with the detected tool/provider versions.
Planned changes and affected resources are understood before authorised application.
Health and recovery checks distinguish prepared, applied and verified states.

specialists.label: Migration, recovery and release completion
specialists.summary: Resume interrupted work from real source and task evidence, preserve milestones and reconcile the requested repository/package/release outcome.
useWhen: The task resumes a stalled build, migrates systems, recovers missing work or completes a release.
Local files, branches, commits, remote repositories or packaged versions disagree.
avoidWhen: There is no migration/release/recovery scope and a normal implementation stage suffices.
acceptance: Task scope is reconciled against actual local, committed, pushed, packaged and deployed revisions.
Authorized significant milestones and next actions are preserved without erasing unrelated work or publishing user media beyond the authorized deliverable and audience.
Remote/package/readback evidence and remaining source, access or environment failures are distinguished explicitly.

specialists.label: Realtime media and native application lifecycles
specialists.summary: Trace message identity, delivery/history, hidden/popout views and shared media ownership through the actual realtime or native runtime.
useWhen: The actual repository uses realtime chat/media, WebRTC, streaming or multi-window state.
A native macOS application or SwiftUI/AppKit bridge is explicitly part of the task.
avoidWhen: A device mentioned in conversation is only the user's computer, not the project target.
The task is static frontend work with no realtime or native lifecycle.
acceptance: Duplicate/retried/reordered messages, acknowledgements, previews and persisted history behave across relevant view/session transitions.
Hidden/popout views retain required subscriptions and shared camera/media owners release resources only at the correct boundary.
Live settings, layout and reconnect/teardown checks identify what ran in a real host versus a simulation.

specialists.label: Reference fidelity and precise corrections
specialists.summary: Preserve approved source identity, constrain changes to requested deltas and verify observable results without collateral redesign.
useWhen: The task reconstructs or adapts supplied HTML, images, screenshots or approved artifacts.
Specific corrections, reference-locked variants or repeated complaints require an item-level delta and preservation checks.
avoidWhen: No reference/preservation requirement affects the change.
The user explicitly requests free exploration; do not impose pixel matching without a source contract.
acceptance: Every correction/target maps to its exact source, allowed change and protected properties.
Comparable before/after evidence shows the named delta and checks retained properties against regression.
Exactness claims state the actual renderer, conditions and comparison result; unavailable visual evidence remains unverified.

specialists.label: Shared design systems, typography and presets
specialists.summary: Maintain canonical components, tokens, fonts, icons and saved visual presets consistently across consumers and interaction states.
useWhen: Shared sections, design tokens, typography systems, icon libraries or component catalogs change.
Theme/accent/font controls, per-section overrides or reusable HTML exports need consistent styling and persistence.
avoidWhen: An isolated illustration has no shared system or consumer contract.
The task changes only local copy and does not need new theme/catalog infrastructure.
acceptance: Changed component families and consumers reconcile with canonical owners and the expected rollout inventory.
Font loading/computed styles and relevant mode/accent/type/interaction/viewport states are actually checked.
Preset change/save/reload/export behavior and standalone component dependencies match their declared contract.

specialists.label: Image art direction and consistent asset production
specialists.summary: Direct authorized image generation/editing with source-locked composition, consistent geometry and semantically distinct product concepts.
useWhen: Product renders, hero/CTA imagery, consistent asset families or precise reference-image edits are requested.
Multiple image concepts or variants need shared-base invariants, meaningful differences and a reconciled output set.
avoidWhen: An exact chart/technical diagram needs deterministic geometry or factual data.
The task implements raster-to-vector conversion rather than generating/editing visual art.
acceptance: Requested assets, dimensions, backgrounds and individual/sheet output forms reconcile with the target matrix.
Reference and output inspection checks geometry, orientation, edges, material detail, composition and protected properties.
Actual image-tool identity/evidence and any fidelity limits are reported without claiming unsupported pixel preservation.

specialists.label: Motion, interactive widgets and temporal verification
specialists.summary: Model and verify meaningful animation sequences, transitions, controls and theme-dependent states over a complete relevant cycle.
useWhen: Animated hero widgets, terminals, maps, carousels, tab cycles or transition defects are in scope.
Pacing, flashing, jumping, barely visible state changes, playback controls or preview clutter affect the requested result.
avoidWhen: The target is static imagery with no temporal behavior.
Only realtime session/resource ownership is involved; use realtime-native.
acceptance: Changed timelines, startup/loop states and relevant controls are observed in the actual supported runtime.
Timing, layout stability, readability and theme states are checked separately from static appearance.
Evidence records output revision and observed cycles; screenshots/builds do not imply temporal verification.

specialists.label: Media libraries, archive ingestion and local conversion
specialists.summary: Extend existing media-workspace navigation, imports, storage and conversion while preserving identity, privacy and measurable fidelity.
useWhen: An HTML/image/icon library, nested ZIP importer, media tree/gallery or large asset workflow changes.
Local conversion, native-pixel comparison, source/preview mapping or media loading performance is a requirement.
avoidWhen: The task creates visual art rather than library/conversion behavior.
A simple one-file export does not involve app integration, ingestion or asset lifecycle.
acceptance: New categories reuse intended shell/tree/import lifecycles and survive reload/navigation/export alongside existing ones.
Requested/imported/duplicate/failed targets reconcile and nested resource links remain valid.
Fidelity/performance/local-only claims are supported by appropriate real comparisons and observations, with actual transport limits stated.

specialists.label: Artifact completeness and verified delivery
specialists.summary: Reconcile complete deliverables, dependency closure, actual output revisions and authorized destination readback before claiming handoff.
useWhen: Multi-file packages, standalone components, archives, asset sets or saved catalog revisions must be delivered.
Import, upload, publication or stale-output complaints require exact target/version and completeness evidence.
avoidWhen: The task is explanation-only with no artifact or delivery requirement.
A format owner still needs to validate the content; packaging alone cannot replace that work.
acceptance: Final artifacts and dependency closure reconcile with the independent requested inventory.
Standalone/opening or clean-extraction checks run in the intended receiving context.
Saved/uploaded/published/observed states identify the same verified output revision, with readback gaps and provider-authenticity limits explicit.

specialists.label: Usage evidence and workflow improvement
specialists.summary: Analyze complete task evidence with deduplication and outcome limits, map demand to current capabilities and evaluate bounded plugin improvements.
useWhen: Usage exports, agent traces or repeated feedback are supplied to improve plugins, skills, routers or workflows.
Existing-versus-missing capability analysis and prioritized evidence-grounded instruction changes are requested.
avoidWhen: The request is ordinary task execution or one local correction already owned by a domain stage.
Unrelated personal-history discovery is not needed or authorized for the current request.
acceptance: All available requested records reconcile with row-level analysis, duplicate/omission handling and reproducible denominators.
Changes map concrete demand to existing/refined/new capability owners while preserving current scope and compatibility.
Sanitized realistic evaluation and private-data exclusion are verified separately from release/host activation.

specialists.label: UI Design Director
specialists.summary: Apply scoped visual corrections and a coherent design direction to every relevant UI task, with complete target review and evidence of visible quality.
useWhen: The actual request creates, changes, reconstructs, reviews or improves a user-visible layout, design, typography, palette, spacing, component presentation, visual asset or motion.
A contextual follow-up asks for visual improvement or corrects prior output, including brief feedback without explicit UI keywords.
A mixed engineering task changes user-facing presentation; apply this lens only to the relevant part and preserve the selected stage boundary.
avoidWhen: The actual task is nonvisual backend, data, infrastructure or source analysis; incidental UI vocabulary does not establish visual scope.
Only a selector or a bare invocation with no recoverable task context is present; identify the actual task before assigning work.
acceptance: Current task, approved source, permitted changes, protected properties and canonical component/token owners determine the design contract before edits.
Every explicitly requested target is visually inspected with its own disposition, defects and improvement opportunities; a sample never becomes an exhaustive review claim.
Rendered appearance, relevant interactions and motion are checked against the actual output revision; structural validation alone is not proof of visual quality.
Native editor work maps to supported kit widgets and authorized exceptions, while project preferences and historical numeric examples remain scoped to their actual context.
